Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.

inventory == 0 and backlog > 0 and pipeline < backlog

candidates.explanation: Demand-responsive: increase orders when recent demand exceeds baseline, but cap increases to avoid overshoot. Decrease when recent demand is below baseline and inventory is positive.
Coordinated node-specific: node0 (downstream) increases orders to meet backlog, node1 (middle) moderates to avoid starving node0, node2 (upstream) increases to replenish pipeline.

rules.when: agent == 1 and backlog > 0 and pipeline < backlog

candidates.explanation: Pipeline-aware relaxation: when pipeline is high relative to recent demand, reduce orders slightly to avoid overstock; when backlog is high, increase orders to clear it. This balances inventory and backlog across all nodes.
Coordinated response to demand surge: increase orders when recent demand exceeds baseline, but cap increases to avoid upstream backlog. Reduce orders when pipeline is excessive relative to demand.
Downstream service protection: prioritize clearing backlog at downstream nodes by increasing orders when backlog is high, while moderating orders when pipeline is already sufficient to meet demand.
